newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila troops disperse students before Congo march.
newsitem.headline: Kabila troops disperse students before Congo march.

text.p: Armed soldiers dispersed hundreds of chanting students on a campus in central Kinshasa on Wednesday, ahead of a banned march called by the main opposition in the Democratic Republic of Congo, witnesses said.

Students fleeing soldiers of self-proclaimed president Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo, formerly Zaire, denounced the presence of Rwandans among Kabila's forces and said foreign troops must return home.
"Kabila should have a chance but we do not want the Rwandans," one woman student told Reuters. "We just do not want the Rwandans. They have got to go."
Dozens of soldiers who arrived in trucks sealed off the campus, preventing students leaving for the central station, the rallying point of the march.
"We are here to bring order, that is all," their commander told Reuters. He declined to give his name.
The campus, the Higher Institute of Commerce, was a hotbed of student opposition to ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.
Kabila, whose forces toppled Mobutu on May 17 after a seven- month civil war, has banned political activity and public demonstrations.
